title: Heat Pump or Solar First in San Diego? (2026)
desc: San Diego has no open utility heat pump rebate, but San Diego Community Power pays $250 to $500 per kWh for batteries. What that means for choosing between them.
h1: Heat Pump or Solar First in San Diego? (2026)
lead: An earlier version of this post said SGIP pays $1,000 or more toward a battery. That is not the program a San Diego homeowner will mostly use now. San Diego Community Power pays $250 to $500 per kWh. Read on October 2, 2026.
sections: For a battery with new solar, SDCP pays $350 per kWh at the market rate and $500 for CARE, FERA or Community of Concern customers. For a battery added to existing solar, $250 and $350. It also pays $0.10 per kWh for evening discharge. For a heat pump, we found no open utility rebate from SDCP or SDG&E. See San Diego solar and battery rebates.

Check the no-cost Equitable Building Decarbonization program first if your income may qualify, since it can include a heat pump and a water heater. If not, a solar and battery system has the clearest published incentive. If a gas heater fails, you will have to decide anyway: get three bids and a written load calculation. San Diego's average January low over 2015 to 2024 was 8.8°C, so most of a heat pump's value is cooling and hot water.
Escondido buys from SDG&E, so the SDCP battery rebate does not apply there. See Escondido.
faq: How much does San Diego Community Power pay for a battery?
$250 to $500 per kWh depending on system type and customer type.
Is there a San Diego heat pump rebate?
We found no open utility rebate. Income-qualified homes can get no-cost upgrades.
